title.narrative: E.A.R.T.H.: Enabling Advancements in Recycling & Transforming Habits through Women-led Initiatives in Jordan

description.narrative:
This project aims to mitigate the adverse environmental consequences resulting from inappropriate waste disposal methods through enabling advancements in recycling, while simultaneously creating employment and livelihood opportunities within the recycling sector for local communities, with a specific focus on vulnerable women. Through the promotion of using recyclable material, waste reuse and recycling practices in the urban context, this project will work to transform habits and mindsets related to waste management and generation.
By increasing public awareness through a targeted campaign, supporting incentives within the recycling sector, and providing training programs for youth and women, this transformation of habits and mindsets encompasses a shift in attitudes, values, and daily routines, leading to long-term changes in behaviour and a collective commitment to adopting more sustainable habits. Incentivizing and rewarding eco-friendly behaviors, such as through increased livelihood opportunities, cash-for-work schemes, and embracing innovative approaches, further motivates individuals and communities to change their habits and embrace more sustainable waste generation and management practices.
The project recognizes the potential of recycling and reuse initiatives in Jordan to drive community empowerment and foster a circular economy, leveraging the skills of the existing informal sector. By establishing a network that includes the HORECA sector (Hotels, Restaurants, and Catering) and building on existing expertise in the informal recycling sector, Jordan can create a comprehensive and sustainable waste management system. These technological advancements position Jordan at the forefront of creating a resilient and inclusive society where women play a vital role as active agents of positive change, contributing to environmental sustainability and the promotion of a circular economy.
In Amman, the project actively engages women in the recycling sector, tapping into an underutilized workforce and providing opportunities for economic empowerment and skill development. Women’s involvement in various aspects of the recycling process, from collection to upcycling, promotes gender equality and inclusivity in the workforce. Embracing a circular economy approach, where materials are recycled and repurposed instead of discarded, Amman can minimize waste, conserve resources, and generate economic opportunities for women, fostering a more inclusive and prosperous society. Furthermore, women play a pivotal role in transforming habits and educating families when it comes to sustainable practices. As influential members of households, they possess a unique position to instill environmentally conscious behaviors within their families. Women can serve as role models, exemplifying sustainable habits like waste reduction, recycling, and energy conservation in their daily lives. Actively engaging in educational initiatives, women can raise awareness about the significance of environmental sustainability, providing valuable knowledge and resources to their families. Their influence as educators extends beyond immediate family members, as they can extend their outreach to extended family, neighbors, and the broader community, cultivating a culture of sustainability.
Overall, the ‘E.A.R.T.H’ project aims to create a ripple effect of positive change, transforming habits, and promoting a more sustainable future for generations to come. It acknowledges the vital role of women in driving this transformation and highlights the potential of recycling, empowerment, and a circular economy in building a resilient and inclusive society in Jordanian cities.
